metadata.title: Why Is TSM Stock Rising Overnight?

content.text:
-
Chip stocks were volatile early Tuesday as investors surveyed updates following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's admission of an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
-
Nvidia is considering slowing chip orders, which would affect upstream supply chain players like TSMC and ASE Technology Holding, according to Commercial Times.
-
TSM stock is down 20% from its October peak.
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSM) shares rose 1% in overnight trading ahead of Tuesday after the Taiwanese contract chipmaker reported a sharp increase in monthly sales. Gains were tempered by controversy surrounding Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy, as well as a report speculating that the AI chipmaker is slowing chip orders.
The go-to chipmaker for Nvidia and Apple (AAPL) said its October revenue rose 60% to NT$586.9 billion ($17.9 billion). That compares to the 51% growth pace in September quarter and 63% growth analysts polled by Bloomberg expect in the current quarter.
Although TSMC's upbeat monthly update is a bullish signal for the chip trader, semiconductor stocks were mixed in early Tuesday hours. NVDA shares were 1% higher after a sharp slide on Monday, while Intel (INTC) was up 0.3% and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) was down 0.4%.
Nvidia Slowing Chip Orders To TSM?
Nvidia is said to be considering slowing chip orders, which would affect upstream supply chain players like TSMC and ASE Technology Holding, a Taiwanese chip assembly and packaging firm, according to a report in the Taiwanese outlet Commercial Times. AMD could be a potential beneficiary.
The developments come amid a volatile period of chip stocks. Last week, TSM fell sharply in tandem with other semiconductor stocks after Democrats, seen to be pro-regulation for AI and data centers, won both the Senate and House in the midterm elections.
TSM stock is now down about 20% from its peak in early October.
Huang, Nvidia Embroiled In Spy Controversy
Nvidia CEO Huang on Sunday admitted to having an affair with a person U.S. authorities suspect to be a Chinese spy. The admission has created a financial shock, with investors panicking that Huang, a key force behind the AI boom, might lose his CEO title.
On Monday, a law firm filed a class action lawsuit against Nvidia and Huang for misleading investors and Delaware senator Chris Coons called for a congressional investigation on national security grounds.
